title: perf: fast path for simple versions (intermediate commit 61967cca)
head: 61967cca278dc51389b8973ba65bbbf23eaa3eda

slower_families.family: Single repeated segment "999." n times plus prerelease c5

Versions with many release segments and a pre‑release suffix (e.g. "1.2.3…a1"). The fast‑path scans the whole string looking for indicator characters, finds the “a”, then falls back to the regex parser – an extra O(n) pass over the input.
Many numeric release segments followed by 'b' pre-release

families.why: The new code first scans the whole string with `_NON_SIMPLE_VERSION_INDICATORS.isdisjoint`. Because the string contains letters such as "a", "b", "c", "r" the fast‑path is not taken, so the extra set‑membership scan is added on top of the original regex match.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated release components before the pre‑release marker; larger n ⇒ longer string and more work for both the indicator scan and the regex.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # build a version like 1.1.1....1.0a1 with n release components
    # release part: n copies of "1." then a final "0"
    release = "1." * n + "0"
    version = f"{release}a1"
    return [[version]]

families.why: Same reasoning as pre‑release: the string contains letters from the indicator set (p, o, s, t, r, e, v) so the fast path is bypassed, incurring the extra `isdisjoint` scan.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated release components before the ".post" marker.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    release = "1." * n + "0"
    version = f"{release}.post1"
    return [[version]]

families.family: versions with a development release segment (e.g. "1.2.3.dev1")
families.why: Contains the letters d, e, v → indicator set not disjoint → fast path skipped, extra scan added.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated release components before the ".dev" marker.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    release = "1." * n + "0"
    version = f"{release}.dev1"
    return [[version]]

families.why: The exclamation mark "!" is in the indicator set, so the fast path is not taken. The epoch number can be made arbitrarily long, increasing the cost of the indicator scan.
families.size_meaning: n = number of digits in the epoch number; larger n ⇒ longer string before the "!" marker.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    epoch = "9" * n          # n‑digit epoch
    version = f"{epoch}!1.0"
    return [[version]]

families.family: versions with a local version segment (e.g. "1.2.3+abc.def")
families.why: The plus sign "+" is part of the indicator set, so the fast path is bypassed. Making the local part longer (more dot‑separated segments) grows the work done by the indicator scan and the subsequent regex.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated alphanumeric segments in the local part.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # local part: n segments like "a", "b", "c" … separated by '.'
    # we cycle through a small alphabet to stay deterministic
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    local = ".".join(alphabet[i % len(alphabet)] for i in range(n))
    version = f"1.0+{local}"
    return [[version]]

families.family: invalid strings that look simple (only digits and dots) but contain a non‑numeric segment, e.g. "1.2.x"
families.why: The indicator set is disjoint, so the fast path is entered. The code then executes `tuple(map(int, version.strip().split('.')))`, which raises `ValueError` on the bad segment; the exception is caught and re‑raised as `InvalidVersion`. Exception handling is considerably slower than the original regex‑only failure path.
families.size_meaning: n = number of leading numeric segments before the bad segment; larger n makes the split and the failed `int` conversion traverse more items before the exception.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # build "1.1.1....1.x" with n numeric parts then a non‑numeric "x"
    good = ".".join("1" for _ in range(n))
    version = f"{good}.x"
    return [[version]]

families.family: Invalid version strings that nevertheless contain indicator characters (e.g. a trailing dot followed by a letter). The fast‑path still does the full scan before the regex fails.
families.why: Even though the version is invalid, the extra disjoint check runs; the regex then fails. This is the single allowed invalid family.
families.size_meaning: Number of dotted segments before the malformed tail.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # "1." repeated n times then an alphabetic tail – not a valid PEP‑440 version
    version = "1." * n + "x"
    return [(version,)]

families.family: Single repeated segment "999." n times plus prerelease c5
families.why: The fast‑path’s `isdisjoint` test iterates over every character. For a long dotted release the string length grows with n, so the extra scan adds linear overhead before the (already linear) regex match.
families.size_meaning: Number of dotted release segments (plus the trailing pre‑release).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    release = ".".join(["999"] * n)
    version = f"{release}c5"
    return [(version,)]

def make(n):
    # Build "1.2.3…n" then add a pre‑release marker "a1"
    release = ".".join(str(i) for i in range(1, n + 1))
    version = f"{release}a1"
    return [(version,)]
